main_body: A dark willow-like tree with a drooping canopy of hanging branches and a flared trunk; the canopy is the largest volume
top_band: none distinct; the canopy top is a ragged organic silhouette of dark brown strands, with no separate flat horizontal band. For an organic tree this is acceptable
evidence: The tree is an organic form with a rounded canopy, a trunk and a flared root base, drawn with a mild top-down tilt like the reference trees. It has no flat planar faces, so the elevation, rim-only and plan failures do not apply. The canopy volume reads as a mass and the trunk as a vertical support beneath it. The contract is only loosely applicable to organic kinds, so I pass it.

style.evidence: The candidate is a drooping, willow-like tree in a very dark brown palette. It has about 3-4 brown steps: near-black, dark brown, mid brown and a few lighter brown highlight dots. The reference canopies carry 5-6 greens with per-leaf-clump highlights. The candidate's strands do give some grain and variation, and the outline is dark brown rather than pure black. But the ramp is compressed and low in contrast, so the canopy reads as a murky mass and not as shaded foliage clumps. The trunk is a mostly flat brown with only a few shading columns, and the base is a thin plinth-like flare. It is next to the reference visibly thinner in shading steps and lower in information density per tile, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
